articles.headline: Kolkata Festival Stampede Leaves at Least 17 Dead
articles.brief: A tragic crowd crush and stampede during a festival in Kolkata, India, has resulted in at least 17 deaths. Authorities and local leaders have launched independent probes, visited victims in hospitals, and promised compensation to the affected families, while police have registered a culpable homicide case.

articles.headline: China Proposes Export Controls on Solar Technologies
articles.brief: China has proposed new export controls targeting crucial solar-manufacturing technologies. The move could significantly impact global supply chains for renewable energy hardware as governments worldwide accelerate their transitions toward clean power generation.

articles.headline: India's HDFC Bank Q2 Net Profit Rises 4.7%
articles.brief: HDFC Bank reported a 4.7% rise in net profit for the second quarter, alongside the announcement that deputy MD Bharucha is set to step down. The results reflect steady banking sector performance amid broader macroeconomic adjustments.

articles.headline: Lithuania Tells Residents to Shelter After Object Detection
articles.brief: Lithuanian authorities advised residents to seek shelter after detecting an unidentified flying object in national airspace. Security forces are actively monitoring the situation amid heightened regional tensions across Eastern Europe.

articles.headline: Ukraine Foreign Minister Calls Russian-Held Town Death Trap
articles.brief: The Ukrainian foreign minister described a Russian-held town as a severe death trap housing starving residents, underscoring the deep humanitarian crisis unfolding in conflict zones as winter approaches and supply lines remain heavily restricted.

articles.headline: Saudi-Led Coalition Reports Helicopter Crash in Najran
articles.brief: A military helicopter crash near the southern border with Yemen killed two crew members, according to the Saudi-led coalition. The incident marks a rare fatality report amid ongoing regional hostilities involving Houthi rebels.

articles.headline: Venezuela Expects $76 Billion in Oil Investment
articles.brief: Acting Venezuelan authorities announced expectations of securing nearly $76 billion in foreign oil investments over the next five years, aiming to revive the nation's battered petroleum infrastructure and boost global supply capacities.

articles.headline: Karnataka Mandates Night Attendance for Doctors
articles.brief: The Karnataka government has made night-time attendance mandatory for doctors serving at taluk hospitals and primary health centers. The order extends to contract and outsourced employees across all government bodies to improve rural healthcare delivery.

articles.headline: Thousands Protest Rising Living Costs Across France
articles.brief: Thousands of demonstrators took to French streets to protest soaring living costs and poor public services, resulting in violent clashes and over a thousand detentions. Student anger merged with union and yellow vest movements, prompting strong condemnation from President Macron.

articles.headline: JD Vance Clarifies H-1B Visa 'Indentured Servants' Remark
articles.brief: US Vice President JD Vance walked back his controversial rhetoric referring to H-1B visa workers as 'foreign indentured servants' following strong protests from India. Vance clarified that his criticism targeted corporate systems rather than individual professionals.

articles.headline: India Drops Sugar-Based Raw Materials from Ethanol Tenders
articles.brief: Oil marketing companies have dropped sugar-based raw materials from the 2026-27 ethanol procurement tender to stabilize domestic sugar availability. The strategic policy shift relies more heavily on grains and molasses to balance local consumption.

articles.headline: Workers in China Train Household Robots for Monthly Pay
articles.brief: Workers across China are recording real-world physical movements and chores to train artificial intelligence robots. Participants earn monthly stipends by teaching machines everyday tasks like folding clothes and sweeping floors.

articles.headline: Health Ministry Confronts Service Trade Deficit Pressures
articles.brief: India's robust services trade surplus faces new tests as faster growth in services imports threatens to erode the financial cushion traditionally offsetting the country's broader merchandise trade deficit, according to recent economic analysis.
